steps.say: Plants need water to stay firm and to make food. Water starts its journey in the soil.

figure.alt: Rain falls on the soil where a plant grows.

steps.say: Roots take in water from the soil. Tiny root hairs help them take in more.
The water travels up tiny tubes inside the stem. The tubes work like very thin straws.
The water reaches the leaves and flowers. Some escapes from the leaves into the air.
You can see this happen. Stand a white flower in coloured water and the petals change colour.

figure.alt: A white flower standing in a glass of coloured water.

steps.say: A plant with no water wilts. Water it, and it becomes firm again.

check.prompt: Which part takes in water from the soil?

options.why: Leaves are in the air, not the soil.
Petals are part of the flower.

hints: Which part grows in the soil?
Think of the part you see when you pull up a weed.
check.explanation: Roots grow in the soil and take in water.

check.prompt: Water travels up the ___ to reach the leaves.
hints: This part is between the roots and the leaves.
It has tiny tubes inside, like straws.
check.explanation: The stem carries water from the roots up to the leaves.
